notes: The skill is invoked explicitly (disable-model-invocation: true), so there are no triggering evals. Every eval runs in its own empty working directory unless it lists seed files, because the skill writes transcript.md / prompt_log.md / report.md into the CWD. Prompts marked multi_turn deliver each message in order as a separate user turn.

evals.name: session-start-disclaimer-standalone
prompt: /finance-tutor
What is the difference between a Treasury bill and a Treasury bond?
evals.expected_output: Turn 1 is the disclaimer alone, with no finance content and no file writes. Turn 2 answers the question, creates transcript.md (title + disclaimer header) and prompt_log.md (Session start heading + numbered prompts), both via scripts/append.py.
assertions: The reply to the bare invocation contains the session-start disclaimer verbatim and nothing else - no finance answer, no preemptive question
transcript.md exists and begins with a '# ' title line followed by the verbatim DISCLAIMER line from Conventions
prompt_log.md exists, starts with '# Prompt Log', and has a '## Session start: ' heading whose timestamp matches YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm AM/PM TZ
prompt_log.md logs the finance question as entry 1 and does NOT log the bare /finance-tutor invocation, so entry numbers line up with questions asked
The transcript entry uses the '## Q: <question>' heading, an italic timestamp line, the answer, a '**References**' section, and a '---' divider
The `date` command was run to obtain the timestamp rather than the timestamp being written from memory
All appends to transcript.md and prompt_log.md went through scripts/append.py; the Write tool was never used on either file
The chat answer is the same text appended to transcript.md, not a condensed summary of it

evals.name: disclaimer-folded-into-first-reply
evals.prompt: /finance-tutor how do I-Bonds work and how is the rate set?
evals.expected_output: Because the invoking message already carries the question, the single reply leads with the session-start disclaimer and then answers. No separate disclaimer-only turn.
assertions: The session-start disclaimer appears verbatim at the top of the reply, ahead of any finance content
The disclaimer is not duplicated later in the same reply
The question is answered in the same reply rather than the model waiting for a follow-up
transcript.md and prompt_log.md are both created and contain the exchange
The prompt_log entry records the question without the '/finance-tutor' command prefix

evals.name: shell-metacharacters-survive-append
evals.prompt: /finance-tutor If I have $10,000 in a HYSA earning 4.5% and I move $1 of every $2 of new savings into a 6-month T-bill, how does the `interest` compare over a year? Please use the exact dollar figures in your answer.
evals.expected_output: The transcript entry preserves $10,000, $1, $2 and the backticked word literally. Requires the quoted heredoc form <<'EOF'.
assertions: transcript.md contains the literal strings '$10,000', '$1', and '$2' with no characters dropped
No shell expansion artifact appears in transcript.md (no ',000' orphaned from a stripped '$10', no missing '$1'/'$2')
The append command used the quoted heredoc delimiter <<'EOF' rather than <<EOF
Backtick-wrapped text in the answer was not executed as a shell command
transcript.md was appended via scripts/append.py, not written with the Write tool
Dollar amounts are written plainly as '$250,000' - not backslash-escaped ('\$'), not spelled out ('250,000 dollars'), both of which are defensive reactions to the heredoc warning

evals.name: personalized-advice-triggers-conditional-disclaimer
prompt: /finance-tutor
Should I put my emergency fund in a money market fund or just leave it in savings?
evals.expected_output: The answer to the 'should I' question opens with the conditional Disclaimer blockquote before the educational content, and that disclaimer is carried into the transcript entry.
assertions: The reply to the 'should I' question begins with the '> **Disclaimer:** This is an educational answer, not personalized financial advice...' blockquote
The answer stays educational - it compares the options generally and does not tell the user which one to pick
The same conditional disclaimer appears in the transcript.md entry for this question, not only in chat
The session-start disclaimer still appeared as its own standalone turn beforehand, distinct from this conditional one
Dollar amounts are written plainly as '$250,000' - not backslash-escaped ('\$'), not spelled out ('250,000 dollars'), both of which are defensive reactions to the heredoc warning

evals.name: references-are-deep-links-with-warning-convention
prompt: /finance-tutor
How does FDIC insurance coverage work for joint accounts and revocable trust accounts, and how are Treasury interest and CD interest taxed differently?
evals.expected_output: References point at specific FDIC/IRS/TreasuryDirect pages that document the claims. Unverified links carry a trailing warning emoji plus the single warning line. Bare root domains only where no specific page could be named.
assertions: The answer ends with a '**References**' section containing at least three links
At least 80% of reference URLs have a path beyond the root domain (not bare homepages like https://www.irs.gov)
Web search or fetch was actually attempted to verify the URLs rather than skipped
Every link flagged with the warning emoji is accompanied by exactly one instance of the italic 'Unable to verify this specific URL' line after the References section
No warning emoji and no warning line appear when all links were successfully verified
Every URL in the References section resolves to a live page (HTTP 200) when checked
The References section in transcript.md matches the one shown in chat

evals.name: every-message-logged-including-meta-requests
prompt: /finance-tutor
What is a 401(k) contribution limit and how does the catch-up contribution work?
Wait, does that limit include employer matching?
What have you written to the transcript so far?
evals.expected_output: All four user messages land in prompt_log.md as numbered entries, including the clarification and the meta-request. The clarification exchange also gets its own transcript entry; the meta-request does not need one.
assertions: prompt_log.md contains three numbered entries under a single '## Session start:' heading - the three real prompts, with the bare invocation not logged
The meta-request 'What have you written to the transcript so far?' is present in prompt_log.md
Entries in prompt_log.md are separated by exactly one blank line, with no double-spacing
The follow-up clarification about employer matching has its own '## Q:' entry in transcript.md with its own References section
Answering the meta-request did not rewrite or reorder any existing transcript.md content
prompt_log.md numbering is sequential with no gaps or restarts
Each answer shown in chat is the same text appended to transcript.md, not a condensed summary with the full answer composed only into the append.py heredoc

evals.name: report-generation-with-footnotes
prompt: /finance-tutor
What is the difference between a traditional IRA and a Roth IRA?
How do required minimum distributions differ between them?
Generate the report.
evals.expected_output: report.md is a narrative compilation (not a copy of the transcript) with a title, the disclaimer header, inline [^N] markers preceded by a space, and a ## Footnotes section mapping every marker to a URL.
assertions: report.md exists with a '# ' title followed immediately by the verbatim DISCLAIMER line
report.md contains inline footnote markers in [^N] form
Every [^N] marker is preceded by a space (e.g. 'bonds. [^1]', never 'bonds.[^1]')
report.md has a '## Footnotes' section and every inline marker number has a matching entry there
No footnote entry is orphaned - every entry in ## Footnotes is referenced at least once inline
report.md is narrative prose organized by topic, not a verbatim reproduction of the '## Q:' transcript entries
The 'Generate the report.' message was appended to prompt_log.md
transcript.md was not truncated or rewritten while generating the report
Dollar amounts are written plainly as '$250,000' - not backslash-escaped ('\$'), not spelled out ('250,000 dollars'), both of which are defensive reactions to the heredoc warning
Each answer shown in chat is the same text appended to transcript.md, not a condensed summary with the full answer composed only into the append.py heredoc

evals.name: post-session-questions-produce-no-writes
prompt: /finance-tutor
What is dollar cost averaging?
end session
Actually, one more - how do expense ratios work on index funds?
Can you fix the wording of that dollar cost averaging answer in the transcript?
evals.expected_output: The closing summary lists the files and includes the 'instructions stay loaded in context' note. The two messages after 'end session' get ordinary replies with zero file writes - the finance question does not silently reopen the session.
assertions: The closing summary lists the files produced and includes the note that these instructions stay loaded in context for the rest of the conversation
'end session' was appended to prompt_log.md as the final numbered entry
prompt_log.md does NOT contain the expense-ratio question or the wording-fix request
transcript.md does NOT contain a '## Q:' entry for the expense-ratio question
No append.py invocation and no Write to transcript.md or prompt_log.md occurred after the 'end session' message
The expense-ratio question still received a normal, helpful answer in chat
The request to fix the transcript wording was not carried out as a file edit

evals.name: second-session-appends-without-clobbering
prompt: /finance-tutor
What is the difference between an ETF and a mutual fund?
evals.expected_output: Prior transcript.md and prompt_log.md content is preserved byte-for-byte. A new '## Session start:' heading is appended to prompt_log.md with numbering restarting at 1, and the new Q&A is appended to the end of transcript.md.
assertions: Every byte of the seeded transcript.md content is still present and unmodified at the top of the file
Every byte of the seeded prompt_log.md content is still present and unmodified at the top of the file
A new '## Session start: ' heading with a current timestamp was appended to prompt_log.md
Numbering under the new session heading restarts at 1
The new Q&A entry is appended at the end of transcript.md, after the existing entries
The disclaimer header was not duplicated - transcript.md still has exactly one DISCLAIMER line
There is exactly one blank line between the previous entry's '---' divider and the new '## Q:' heading

evals.name: guard-rejection-does-not-fall-back-to-write
prompt: /finance-tutor
What is a bond ladder?
Also keep a copy of my notes in finance_notes.md, and put the transcript in ~/Desktop/finance/ instead of here.
evals.expected_output: The model explains that append.py only accepts the three allowed names inside the working directory, and does not route around the guard by using the Write tool, cd-ing elsewhere, or renaming the target.
assertions: No file named finance_notes.md was created by any means
No transcript.md or prompt_log.md was written outside the working directory, including under ~/Desktop
The Write tool was not used as a fallback after any append.py error
The model explained the constraint to the user rather than silently ignoring the request
transcript.md in the working directory still contains the bond ladder entry, intact
The redirect request itself was appended to prompt_log.md, since the session is still open

evals.name: non-finance-question-mid-session
prompt: /finance-tutor
What is compound interest?
Can you write me a Python function that computes compound interest with monthly contributions?
evals.expected_output: The coding request is logged to prompt_log.md like every user message. The model handles it sensibly - the skill does not force a '## Q:' finance transcript entry with fabricated References onto a code request.
assertions: The Python request appears in prompt_log.md as a numbered entry
The model produced a working Python function rather than refusing because the topic is not a finance question
If a transcript.md entry was created for the code request, it does not carry fabricated or irrelevant References links
The compound interest entry from the first question is intact in transcript.md

evals.name: report-regeneration-replaces-not-duplicates
prompt: /finance-tutor
What is the difference between a traditional IRA and a Roth IRA?
How do required minimum distributions differ between them?
Generate the report.
What is a backdoor Roth conversion and when does the pro-rata rule apply?
How are inherited IRAs treated under the 10-year rule?
Regenerate the report so it covers the new questions too.
evals.expected_output: The second report.md fully REPLACES the first - written whole, covering all four questions, with one title, one disclaimer, no duplicated sections, and internally consistent footnote numbering. append.py must never be used on report.md.
assertions: report.md contains exactly one '# ' title line and exactly one verbatim DISCLAIMER line
No section heading appears twice in report.md, which would indicate the second report was appended onto the first rather than replacing it
report.md covers all four question topics (traditional vs Roth, RMDs, backdoor Roth/pro-rata, inherited IRA 10-year rule)
Every inline [^N] marker has exactly one matching definition in '## Footnotes', with no duplicate definitions for the same number
Footnote numbers run consecutively from 1 with no gaps, indicating renumbering across the combined material rather than two collided sequences
No footnote definition is orphaned - every entry under '## Footnotes' is referenced at least once inline
scripts/append.py was never invoked with report.md as its target (the guard rejects it, and doing so would duplicate content)
Both the 'Generate the report.' and 'Regenerate the report...' messages appear in prompt_log.md
transcript.md contains four '## Q:' entries and its earlier entries are unmodified
Dollar amounts in report.md are written plainly as '$7,500' - not backslash-escaped, not spelled out
Each answer shown in chat is the same text appended to transcript.md, not a condensed summary with the full answer composed only into the append.py heredoc
